requirements.evidence: Default map + range fallback in Queue::defaultPrefixFor (app/Models/Queue.php:47-54); custom map wins in prefixForPriority (Queue.php:39-42); key/value/effective-uniqueness validation and empty->null in normalizePrefixMap, run in a saving hook (Queue.php:27-31, 69-99) throwing InvalidArgumentException; array cast + not in #[Fillable]. Migration adds issue_date nullable, backfills DATE(issued_at), ->change() to NOT NULL, swaps unique to (queue_id, code, issue_date), with down() (2026_10_29_055508...php:18-44). nextCode filters by queue, issue_date and prefix, orders by id, skips malformed codes via '^P(\d{3,})$' (Ticket.php:38-54). IssueTicket reads `$now = now()` once and uses it for code day, issued_at and issue_date (IssueTicket.php:27,46-58). Factory sets issue_date from issued_at before allocating a code with the ticket's priority/day and keeps explicit codes (TicketFactory.php:45-67). UpdateQueue gets `?array $priorityPrefixMap = null`, validates before any change and maps errors to ValidationException key priority_prefix_map (UpdateQueue.php:21-34, 69-71). The issue_date date cast is present, and business-rules, database-schema and CHANGELOG are updated.

conventions.evidence: The domain write goes through the UpdateQueue action, which authorizes first with Gate::forUser($actor)->authorize('update', $queue). Mass-assignment is kept deliberate: priority_prefix_map is not added to #[Fillable], and a test asserts this (QueuePriorityPrefixTest.php:62-64). Migrations have generator-style timestamps/names and reversible down(). PHPDoc on new public methods; docs/business-rules.md 'Display code' section, docs/database-schema.md ER + notes, CHANGELOG [Unreleased] updated. Style matches siblings (Pest it(), RefreshDatabase, action invocation).

security.evidence: Map is not mass-assignable and is changed only via UpdateQueue, which authorizes before validating; employees and outsiders are denied (UpdateQueuePrefixMapTest.php:75-92). Strict validation (canonical integer keys, /^[A-Z]$/ values) also makes the interpolation of $prefix into LIKE and the regex in Ticket::nextCode safe. No UI/Livewire or output surface touched.

tests.evidence: New tests cover: default/range prefixes, custom map precedence, empty->null on every save, non-fillable, invalid keys/values/duplicate effective letters via datasets (QueuePriorityPrefixTest.php); independent prefix sequences, legacy A codes, daily restart, midnight boundary and single clock read (IssueTicketPrefixTest.php); factory issue_date default and backdated allocation (TicketFactoryPrefixTest.php:25-43); migration backfill + NOT NULL + new unique key (TicketIssueDateMigrationTest.php); UpdateQueue store/omit/clear/invalid-unchanged/unauthorized (UpdateQueuePrefixMapTest.php). Existing tests are updated from A to N codes, which the new spec requires; none are weakened.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly lean: nextCode keeps the existing scan-by-id approach and only adds filters; the single normalizePrefixMap is reused by the saving hook and by UpdateQueue. Minor extras: the factory re-queries the queue with Queue::query()->findOrFail (TicketFactory.php:61) on every make, and UpdateQueue's normalized value is normalized again by the saving hook. The issueDate set-mutator (Ticket.php:61-64) adds code but is justified by the date cast's storage format.

readability.evidence: Clear names (prefixForPriority, defaultPrefixFor, normalizePrefixMap, issueDate). Comments explain non-obvious decisions (single clock read, IssueTicket.php:25-27; Y-m-d storage, Ticket.php:56-60; validate-before-mutate, UpdateQueue.php:25). Methods are small, and there is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: All edits serve the task. The docs/api/totem.md example/description update (slug 'P012', per-day uniqueness) is a docs-in-sync change the conventions call for. No unrelated refactors.

issues.explanation: The old unique(queue_id, code) is dropped before the new (queue_id, code, issue_date) index is created (same in down()). On MariaDB, if that index is the only one backing the queue_id foreign key, the drop can fail with 'needed in a foreign key constraint'. Creating the new index first avoids this.
The factory runs an extra findOrFail query per ticket to get the queue, even when the related model is already set on the ticket ($ticket->queue).
`migrate:rollback --step 1` assumes this migration is always the latest one, so the test breaks silently once a later migration is added.
The `(string) (int) $key !== $key` check mostly repeats the canonical-integer regex. A short comment saying it guards against integer overflow would make its purpose clear.

review.summary: The change adds priority-letter ticket codes that restart daily per queue and per letter. It covers the per-queue validated prefix map (normalized on every save, managed through the authorized UpdateQueue action), the issue_date column with backfill and a new unique key, single-clock issuance, factory alignment, docs and changelog. It covers every requirement and the contract, and the tests are thorough and meaningful. The main nit is the index swap order in the migration, which could fail on MariaDB, so I would approve with nits.
